newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Qantas to raise fares 2.5 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Qantas to raise fares 2.5 pct - paper.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd would increase its domestic passenger fares by around 2.5 percent from Wednesday, The Australian newspaper reported on Tuesday.
Qantas' main competitor, Ansett Australia, was likely to follow Qantas later this week and raise its fares, the newspaper said.
A Qantas spokesman was not immediately able to comment on the report.
Qantas was also considering a similar increase for some of its international fares because of the 40 percent surge in jet fuel prices this year, the newspaper said.

The world's airlines, desperate to hold up their profits in the face the rise in fuel prices, said in Geneva last week through the International Air Transport Association (IATA) that they proposed to raise passenger fares by three percent.
IATA, which has 251 member airlines, said in Geneva the proposed increase, which is subject to government approvals, would apply to fares from December 15.

Qantas, 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc, announced last week that it planned to introduce a 12 Australian cents a kilogram surcharge on long haul international freight rates to compensate for higher fuel costs.
Ansett is jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd.
